items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1983-05-28
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Joyce Lewis; the interviewer mentions Joyce Lewis in the context of other musicians who didn't mind playing at informal gatherings.

ctx.x: I used to wonder a little bit about how legitimate a function it was and whether or not the band was being taken advantage of. Because, well, because you invite somebody to a party and tell them to be sure to bring his horn, there's some kind of suggestion that may be, well.

Well, they certainly didn't mind doing it. I think at times they didn't have many jobs, even people like Joyce Lewis. Yeah. There was a chance for them to get together and play. That's true. It certainly wasn't a rehearsal. No, it wasn't. Did you go to rehearsals ever?

I don't, I probably have gone to a rehearsal. I've gone more to auditions than I have to a rehearsal. Yeah. I know on several occasions I was notified by one person or another that a particular group, well, it seems to me that you had one for Billy. Billy and Dee Dee Pierce and their group in the back of the New Orleans record shop. I'll pass the leader.

items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-01
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...one of the leading lights said, Joyce Lewis and Paul Barberin don't play jazz...

ctx.x: Looked like it was one of these unintentional non-profit organizations. Mm-hmm. Yeah.

Yeah, but, uh, well my feeling was that we were somewhat considered outcasts, and I would, uh, I can remember going to a meeting of people who collected records, supposedly, and really liked them, and one of the leading lights said, Joyce Lewis and Paul Barberin don't play jazz, they play Creole music, which I found a bit weird. But, uh, you know, you're full of people, the world is full of people like that.
